newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Bank Hapoalim rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Bank Hapoalim rated a buy.

text.p: Sahar Securities and Investments maintained its buy recommendation for Bank Hapoalim despite what it said was a slightly lower than forecast fourth- quarter profit.
The bank announced earlier this month that fourth-quarter net profit rose to 122 million shekels from 106 million shekels in the same period a year ago.
"Bank Hapoalim's fourth-quarter results are slightly lower than we anticipated," said the report by analyst Doron Tsur. "We do not attach great significance (to this)."
It said most of the difference stemmed from a non-recurring employee bonus for the bank's 75th anniversary and a decision to accelerate a state-mandated provision for doubtful debt.

"The banking commissioner forced the banks to make a provision on account of what was defined as 'unidentified risks in the client liabilities portfolio' and to reach a certain goal by 1999, defined as a percentage of the client portfolio," the report said.

"The bank decided to accelerate the rate of provision and to reach this goal by the end of 1996...the expenditure on account of this item consequently grew from 23 million shekels in 1995 to 193 million shekels in 1996."
Sahar said it was maintaining its buy recommendation despite the share's 39 percent rise since Sahar's previous recommendation last December.

"We estimate the suitable price for the bank's share to be 8.25-8.5 shekels, according to a forecasted EPS (earnings per share) of 0.7-0.75 shekels (in 1997), and a P/E (price/earnings ratio) of 11-12," the report said. The shares are currently trading at 6.97 shekels.
Sahar said Hapoalim shares are the most attractive in the sector since other Israeli banks are trading at relatively higher prices.
